title: Dave Canales: 'There’s Work to Do' | Carolina Panthers
text: Uh just a great byee uh time of connection early on in the week being able to talk to the coordinators and uh the goal is what are we doing well? What needs improvement? Um just diving into some of those things and trying to find an edge whatever that might be for us. So um and then on top of that just the early byee comes in um in a timely fashion with some guys you know battling their way to get back and and some guys that have been out for a little while that um that may have an opportunity and for their windows to open up. Uh, and then as a as we got closer to the weekend, you know, just a great time to spend with family, um, with my wife Lizzie and the kids, um, all the other coaches and players as well. Some cool stuff. Big congrats to Rob Hunt getting married this weekend. Um, that's all public news. So, uh, the guys were fired up about that today in the team meeting. But, um, you know, this week has been about connection. This week has been about, um, just being, you know, everybody, let's just let's just put our heads together and let's find a way to, uh, find this consistency that we're looking for. All right, we'll start with Mike followed by Joe. >> Hey Dave, good afternoon. >> Hey Mike. >> Um, as far as Turk, Taylor, Turk and Taylor are concerned, but also Brady and Bam. How what does it look like with your injury situation heading into this week? >> Yeah, I'll give a a much clearer update on that um later on in the week, but you know um right now the the window starts to open up for these guys. I'm really excited. They're excited to get back out there. We got to get them some football to kind of be able to evaluate their availability um in the next couple of weeks. >> I know you don't want to disclose kind of strategic stuff, but will you open up their windows this week as far as >> Yes. Yes, we'll open up Turk and Teemo's window this week for sure. And then we'll how we do that, how they respond to the work. We'll give all that information later. >> But Trevor is definitely coming off IR as you said last week. >> Yes. >> Thank you. Hey Dave, good to see you. >> Hey Joe, >> hope you had a goodbye. Um, where where to Taylor's concerned? Uh, how key is that uh with the potential that uh that Monroe could is a little dinged up with the knee. >> I mean, it's timely certainly, you know, and and Monroe is doing everything he can uh to make himself available for this week. Again, we'll take we'll go through that process. And um of course Teemo, you know, hasn't seen football. Um he's he looks in great shape. Um he's ready to go. He's been cleared medically. Um but now it's going to be about the football and that's what this week is about. >> And then Turk, obviously you you guys have have made improvements in the run defense for sure, but getting him back potentially. Uh what does that do for the defense and the run defense in particular? Yeah, it can be a real uh breath of fresh air and just kind of um first and foremost, let's just talk about from a personal standpoint, you know, um he's worked so hard to get back to this point. We were so fired up to get that information earlier uh to be able to be cleared to get back to playing football. And he brings in energy, he brings in excitement whether it's in practice and especially the games. And uh it'll be very um very interesting to see how we're able to, you know, factor him back into to a role. Um, but all that stuff will make sense the more we see what what his uh physical readiness is. >> Yep. >> We'll go to Alex followed by Jeff. >> Hey Dave, how's it going man? >> Hey Alex. >> Hey. Um, I [clears throat] respecting the fact that you don't want to give too much info about injury situations until tomorrow. Uh, but uh with Jaylen Phillips, what can you say about his status at the moment? And then also, what does he bring to the run defense that perhaps doesn't show up on the stat sheet like, you know, sacks do and pressures do? >> Yeah. Um, first of all, you know, Jaylen's got a chance. Um, again, we'll get into more specifics about that, but um, you know, the biggest thing that Jaylen brings is just his motor. Um, he's a powerful man. He's huge. You know, he goes, you know, close to 270 lbs at 6'5 and he can really run. So whether he's on the front side or backside of a run, he's a problem, um, for opponents. And so, um, we love that about him. We love the way he attacks it that way. And then, um, you know, certainly a guy that's, uh, you know, he's an every down player and he can be out there, um, he's certainly impactful in pass rush, but to be able to have that stout, uh, point of attack, uh, on first and second down now, whether it's run or play actions, those types of things. Um, you know, he's a critical part of what we're doing. >> And then I got a more general question. Um, it was a massive win. Sunday Night Football on prime time all bye-week there was uh, you know, national media was talking about Bryce Young for MVP and how great the Panthers are at this point in the season. Um, what is the challenge of having to refocus the team after a week in which y'all got so much, you know, public approval, so to speak? I think it's critical that we just take it one week at a time and the goal is to improve weekly to find things, find areas that need our attention and it usually comes back to the fundamentals that always brings us back to work. Whether it's after a a great win like the Sunday night win, whether it's after a loss, the thing that brings us back and grounds us is that there's work to do. We have another amazing opponent in the Philadelphia Eagles this week. That should be enough. And then of course having the ability to go through our self scout and look at the areas that we can improve um tremendously then it's there's a way that just that'll humble a group that'll make that'll sharpen our focus so that we can be clear about what it is. You know it can't be about um it can't be about anything bigger than just taking the next step this week. Again, we sell championship opportunity every single week, especially against a really well-known NFC opponent like the Eagles, um, and the type of football that they're capable of. So, it's going to require all of our focus going into the Lions game. I've said up here, I've said to the team that was our best week of prep, a group working together for multiple weeks, problem solving, finding fundamentals, talking to each other, honing our skills, all those things. We have to be able to replicate that type of a week to get the consistent type of fl of play that's out there for us, you know. And while there may be buzz from one game, we've had other opportunities in in different games throughout this season that'll show guys we we really still have a lot to improve on, a lot to really commit our focus to. >> Uh, greetings. Uh, can you hear me, Dave? >> I got you. >> Trust you had a good by week. >> Oh, yeah. Uh, good. I got a question on the safeties. Uh, Wheelley entered the by-week as the second highest gradeated rookie and Ranson continues to prove to be a big hitter. Uh, Trayvon and Nick have endured their up and downs this season. Um, is there a changing of the guard in the safety room? >> You know, having Nick back on Sunday night was critical to our success. the way that he communicated. When I talk about the week of preparation, I'm talking about Nick Scott, talking about the way that he was in the middle of the group tying guys together. Um, getting two corners, Will Lee, Caleb Evans to really connect that whole back half, um, and tie the unit together. So, can't talk about the safeties without talk about Nick and certainly Trey's impact. Um, the way that he's been, uh, playing against the run the last couple of weeks has been incredible. I'm really fired up about Zigg. I'm really fired up about Lean. the way that those guys are really taking to the game plan, showing up and making plays, open field tackles, big hits. You know, I think about uh Lean's hit on Gibbs to knock the ball free. Um that was they were closing down in the red zone was critical in and minimizing that drive to a field goal. So, um these guys we it's a good room and I love the competition. That's right at the heart of what Dan and I believe is let's continue to bring great players into these rooms to challenge our roster in different ways. And so, um, and it's, you know, of course it's E's job to find a way to get all those guys involved, which is a challenge, but at the same time, these guys can have roles and they can help their team. >> On offense, uh, thanks for that, by the way. Um, on offense, uh, Chuba >> had at least three significant runs, uh, with Young taking snaps under center, uh, including the opening, uh, touchdown. Is the offense leaning more toward taking snaps under the center? >> Well, we like the balance. Um, the good part about being under center, your your runs, first of all, can hit a little bit more direct. Uh, gives Chuba, gives the guys an ability to kind of press the hole a little bit longer, make their decision. But it's also the pass game that comes off of it. When you're under center, there are a lot of variables. When you're in the gun offset, there are only a couple directions the ball can really go, but when you're in the dot, it can go either way in a bunch of different play styles, play types, and then it's the action that comes off of it. you get more of a drastic run type of effect with that mesh. Quarterback's back is turned to the defense. That opens up potential explosive passes on the back half. So, it's got to be a part of what we do. Um, I don't want to say it's going to be more that over gun versus pistol. That'll be a week- toeek thing depending on what we're what's available and what the defense is presenting to us, but it's always been a part of what we've done since I've gotten here. It'll continue to be that. >> Hey, thanks. Good luck. >> You're welcome. Thanks, Jeff. We'll go to Scott followed by Eric. >> Uh, hey Dave, some crazy games yesterday. I'm >> curious how much of that you watched and given the results. If you bring up the fact that you guys are now alone in first place to the team or is that something you try to ignore? >> Uh, that was something we addressed. Our the goal of our whole group is to win the division. Um, is to win the NFC South. That's a collective vision, a collective thing we're striving to. Let's win the first championship first. It's playing out really nicely. It has nothing to do with how we perform. We have to get back to the basics. We have to find consistency in our run game on the offensive side. Defensively speaking, making sure that we're able to corral the quarterback and contain it in our rush. We're getting great pressure. Let's make sure that it stays that way and we recontain that way. Some communication things with the with the coverage units and all that. continuing to build our blitz packages. All these things that we've been talking about improving, that's got to be the focal point. And so, while those things play out yesterday, we're fired up about that, but it's going to be about us preparing the right way for the Eagles this week. Um, but, you know, I think just as you bring it up, you know, none of us can ignore those games. It's a great opportunity in a by-week to be able to, you know, pop on the red zone, try to see as much as possible. I had to go back because I'm getting texts from coaches, you know, just about did you see what happened here? Did you see this, you know, this type of management, this decision to do this here? Did you see this player, you know, reach the ball out in a situation? Didn't call for it. And all these things, these are examples that we like to show our guys. And we didn't sit there and watch a whole cut up, but Tracy did a great job just kind of going through a weekend review of the different special teams plays that impacted the game just to get the guys snap back into our decision- making and where we need to go as a unit. And last one for me. Speaking of that, I I assume you had a chance to watch the Eagles given that they were playing in a slot by themselves and there and they had a special teams uh thing at the end that influenced of course everything. Um when a team loses a heartbreaker like that, do you think it matters, you know, in terms of how they're going to come out Sunday? >> I certainly think it there's a there's a an an urgency, there's a response. Um we've been in those situations um coming off of tough losses, being able to show the critical moments in the game that led to losing this opportunity. Um and it heightens uh the impact of the things that we're trying to fix. Um coaches over the years have said, you know, like when you win, sometimes if you're not careful, the lessons learned can get watered down, can get brushed aside. But when you lose, it heightens it. It brings everything under a microscope. And that's the way you should approach approach it always. Um, but there is a response and and I'm expecting that the Eagles will look at some of those moments, you know, and and even just kind of as these last couple of games have stacked up against them, this is a really talented football team with a lot of good X's and O's happening there. Um, and I'm expecting them to be at their best. I'm expecting them to address those things and and bring their best, you know, when we go out there to Philly. So, for me, that helps me be able to sell the urgency to the team, how important our prep is, how important this day is, because now you got a team that's hungry. We can't make it about them, but you can certainly expect that we're going to get their best. >> Thanks, Dave. >> Dave, what's going on? How are you? >> Hey, how you doing? >> Good, man. Good. Um, obviously, uh, the interior on the, uh, Eagles side with Jaylen Carter and Jordan Davis, two of the best combo or one of the best combos in the league. Uh, what are you hoping that Joe and the O line room really focus on, uh, in preparation this week? Yeah, we have a bunch of things uh to emphasize first and foremost for our own schemes and then how does that fit in with the style of how they play and um and you got to be aware of, you know, where where those guys are at all times and how you're hitting the combos, looking at all the different teams who have found success, what did they do, how can we try to take advantage of some of those things. Um but they're great players and they're going to make their plays and the important part is can we look at it as as not necessarily, hey, we can't run this run anymore. were our fundamentals in the right place to be able to make sure that the the first level of the defense is covered up so we can create movement in that in that regard. >> And this one might be a little bit more cerebral, but there's not many uh places and buildings or fan bases that uh influence a game more than Philadelphiaians. Um what's something maybe a conversation you've had uh with the players in the sense of maybe not getting too hot or not being influenced so much by the crowd because again they can definitely get a little rowdy out there. Yeah, it's a championship opportunity and you know the further you get into the season and the more critical games are, you're going to face environments like this and it's about us. It's about making sure that we we stay within ourselves. We celebrate with each other. We know we're going to have a handful of Panthers fans that are going to show up for us and we're fired up to see them. what we're counting on is each other on the sideline, the coaches in the locker room, the adjustments, creating our own energy and staying together for however long it takes. And so, um, these types of opportunities, these types of championship moments get you prepared for these critical games as you go into it. And, you know, the further you get into the playoffs, the better the environment gets. And we were able to see that firsthand what it felt like to be able to play that wild card round at home. It means the same thing for other teams as well. And especially when you're finishing the season, trying to win that division, a couple of those critical games that start to happen, let's practice that now. Let's have our minds clear. Let's be focused. Let's be locked in and connected to each other. >> Awesome. Thank you. >> All right, we'll go to Cassidy followed by Nick. >> Hey Dave, how's it going? >> Hey Cass, >> um, we've seen Lee Hunter really kind of come into his own both on the field and off the field personalitywise. How do he and DB kind of balance each other, I guess, both on and off the field since they seem to be two very different personalities, different styles? Like what what kind of can they create together? And what has that been like to watch? Yeah, I mean what I've learned about Derek is um while Derek can be vocal, he has great words usually to say in a challenging way um in a way of confidence, bringing confidence to our team, uh to the locker room. And what I'm learning more and more about Lee Hunter and you know, particularly even on Sunday night, just the the more comfortable he gets with playing our techniques, um knowing where he's supposed to be, hitting blocks the right way, getting off of them and trying to make plays. I'm starting to see his personality. I mean, he it's funloving, you know, and Dererick is a very serious competitor. He's focused. He's locked in. Um, pretty menacing looking. And and for Lee, you know, there's just this energy that he brings, um, this joy for the game, this joy, um, and connection with his teammates that's really starting to emerge. Um, and when I see guys start to emote that way, when I start to see personality, the more important lesson for me is, oh, that means he knows what he's doing in all the other stuff. And that's a part of growth, especially for rookies, where the more comfortable you are in our schemes, our calls, and our technique, the more we get to see your personality start to take shape um and start to really affect your team. And I'm glad it's trending that way for Lee. As you can imagine, the first four weeks, man, this game is fast. The things move. They're trying to attack the fronts in different ways. And as you kind of get used to it and you get and you get used to the the fundamentals that coach Wash is talking about and and that discipline uh performance. Okay, now it's not now we start to see the personality and I'm excited to see that. >> And then one other just real quick one. This is a defensive system for the Eagles that mirrors EJ's a lot just having learned from Vic. Is there something you can pull from that just having faced it every day in practice? >> Yeah, absolutely. It helps uh the whole group being able to know um how different techniques are played at every level up front by the linebackers and certainly in the secondary um what leverages they like to play to and what things might look like right before the snap. Though all those things help and then of course just going through a full self scout to see our defense function to see how teams try to attack us. You know there there were some really good conversations that carry over and do help uh the initial part of the game plan. Good afternoon, Dave. Um, what did you like about the run game against Detroit? And as you go into this portion of the season, how important is it going to be to fold that back into the identity of the offense? >> I believe it's critical to be able to have a run game we can depend on. It opens things up. Um, it also just allows for an offense to control the game when your run game is putting you into those second and manageable situations where the whole call sheet is open for Brad. Um, it opens up explosive passes. When Chuba gets going like he did and he's starting to break tackles and rip off bigger runs, you gain more attention. The play passes become more critical. Um, I also like just a little bit of the run variety, different styles of run types. So, it's not the same thing the whole time. We can hit our our system, we can hit the core of what we do, but then there's compliments off of it. Um, that allows you to protect. And that's not just with the run game, but that's also with the pass game. protecting your core by having variety off of the same looks and those types of things. That's all of our responsibilities as coaches. >> And we're talking last night on Sunday night about Derrick Henry and a bigger back being able to heat up late in the game. I know Chupa is not Dererick Henry's size, but is he does he have that kind of attribute late in the game? >> Yeah. Um it just it's about his preparation. about Chuba's fitness, uh his body care, um his attention to studying what the defense is trying to do, knowing what they're going to go to in a four-minute mode. Um seeing the different types of uh defensive players he's playing against and how they approach tackling. All those things matter. Chuba puts in the work. The more Chuba touches the ball, the more comfortable he gets. And he's able to take advantage of some of those things. but he's done such an incredible job um this year of just making sure that he's got readiness for game day. And Chuba is an overworker um to a fault because he cares because he's going to go a million miles per hour as long as we let him. And there's been this really good give and take of making sure you got enough to be ready for Sunday, but let's not overdo it because Sunday is the show and that is the day where we need you to be fully fresh and all that. and and um you know with with JB out for a little bit of time, AJ popping in there, Trey kind of stepping in, Chuba's given us that consistency to be able to hit those runs so we have good film to watch. Doing it just right so we can grow this thing as we go. >> Awesome. And we'll wrap things up with Steve. >> Hey Dave, hope your uh bye-week was went well. >> Thanks Steve. Um, hey, uh, you talked about one Jaylen, but I wondered if, uh, you could just kind of give us an update on the other Jaylen, Jaylen Coker. Um, how'd he come out of the bye-week? Um, is he trending towards, you know, possibly getting back on the field? >> Yeah, he he had a great bye-week. Um, you know, just continuing to ramp up every day with some rest in there as well. Um, all these guys have been going hard, you know, all across the league really since training camp and you get into the first four weeks of the season and um, and you're just you're just hit with different loads. um and different spikes in exertion and high-speed mileage and all these different things that we're keeping track of. But um Jaylen's on track. He's got a couple of big days ahead of him. Um I'll give you more information as the week goes on, but um we'll get a great opportunity tomorrow to get on the field and uh and to take a look at some things and then and then see if we can continue to progress. [music] >> [music]

title: Todd Monken Press Conference | October 12th, 2026
text: Good idea. We'll start with you expect to practice this week. >> Uh I think there there is a possibility we'll open up his window uh for this week. >> Okay. The second one is I know you know what a good running game looks like. You said if you had the answers you fix it. Is it as simple as the last or is it something more than that five games in >> um you feel like you have the >> Well, it's not just one thing. I said it last night. Uh having Derek and Lamar obviously is advantageous just like having Deshaawn in his legs and uh having Quinn Shawn Judkins uh it it's never just one thing. Uh it's scheming, it's uh it's us running off the football. It's executing at a much higher level than we are right now. And uh till we do that, we will struggle. And it really wasn't that way at Pittsburgh. I thought felt like we had made some strides and you know the Jets have a good front and we just didn't uh didn't execute and certainly didn't uh didn't coach it well enough injury there's a number of guys who didn't play with thisbody against the Ravens or unlikely I don't know that yet. I don't I don't see anybody at this point that uh that I know for sure will be out. >> Yeah, I'd say daytoday. He did. He had a little tweak in his ankle and precautionary. We put him in a boot. I would I would say he's day to day. >> Got one last question on the running the running game. you guys operating your offense out of shotgun. You have the fewest number of runs from under center. Why is that? And is that something that you're running the ball that you know in the weeks to come? Well, we're still trying uh to figure out in a lot of ways who we are um offensively uh what our strengths are and what our weaknesses is as players, as as collectively, as a staff. So, um we're always under construction and that's always subject to change in terms of what we feel like gives us the best uh chance to move the ball, run or pass. Next, we'll >> go to Mary K. Yeah, coach, you wanted to reserve judgement last night on how you thought Deshawn Watson played until you watched the film and uh you know obviously it was a challenging game for everyone, but did it look any better, any worse, the same as what did you see of Deshawn when you film today? >> Well, I think collectively as an offense, we did not handle the elements very well. It was difficult on both teams. I'm sure there's there's elements of their offense, the Jets, that they would look at it and say they didn't handle it very well, whether it's holding on to the ball or the penalties they had. It's the same with us. And the team that handled it the best was going to give themselves an upper hand. And I just think collectively Deshaawn being a part of that. I don't think we handled uh the elements uh as well as we could have. And uh we certainly uh that showed up and I'm sure Deshawn will say he certainly can play better and we can certainly play better around him. Yeah, coach wanted to ask you about the offensive line and the volume of sacks and quarterback hits allowed yesterday was when you went back and looked at it on the film, how much was that a product of Deshawn's mobility and extending plays versus you know break down up front. >> All the above. I mean, um I would say that the starting point is one getting the ball out when we don't have answers. Uh the other is our communication up front that we're on the right people and missed assignments. There was a couple times where we might have just gotten beat, but the collective part was more get the ball out and communication and that was that was what was most uh frustrating. >> And I want to ask you about Isaiah Bond. He had such a strong offse training camp, pre-season. Um just what do you think happened yesterday? Was it as simple as the ball was wet and was slipping through his hands? >> I don't know. You'd have to ask Isaiah. I mean, it's unfortunate. uh they had to deal with the elements like we did. Uh we certainly had a couple other drops uh within that. Um but collectively as an offense, we have got to play cleaner and it's next man up and and we didn't do that collectively. Um whoever came in the game and our skilled players uh being able to execute at a high level and uh and it showed. >> Thanks for Scott. Todd, following up on that, like as a coach, how do you handle when you have multiple shots in a game? Is there anything you can do or say? >> No, I mean other than it happened sporadically throughout the game, so it's not like you're, you know, one of them was near the end and the other ones it's I mean it I think these guys have been doing it long enough it's hard to really get into, you know, the mechanics of of catching a football at that point. And again, we we collectively did not handle the elements very well. Um, and they did a good job defensively against us. So, that's what it's going to look like when Browns hurt Browns and when you're not clean in terms of your operation handling the elements. And that's that's what happened yesterday. And as as good as we felt in some ways the previous Thursday, this is part of what you go through. This is the NFL. This is a week-toeek league. And we certainly didn't put our best foot forward offensively yesterday. And our job is to get it cleaned up here today and then come back on Wednesday and and work like hell to get it fixed. That's what we're going to do. >> And what did you see out of your tackle group? >> Man, it was those guys uh that got elevated really gave us some valuable minutes. And Sam, you can see what a valuable piece Sam has been around here, you know, with his back issues and then coming back and just chomping at the bit to get an opportunity to play and he really showed up in a big way. >> Tony, I want to go back to the shotgun versus under center discussion. Is it a matter of you and your staff trying to max out of the shotgun at the risk of giving something away in the running game? >> I don't know. I mean, there's there's a little of everything that goes with it. I mean, certainly uh we're certainly capable of pivoting what we feel like is best for us moving forward. There's more to it than just that, but um you know it, you know, we were playing Tampa four weeks ago and we were under center and they were pressuring us and then we got in the gun and and we had some success and we were running it and we're throwing it. We're getting the ball out of his hands and each week you're pivoting. It's um you want to have enough in your offense uh to not be pigeonhold as to one way to be able to move the football and and we're certainly it's it's not in stone, it's in sand and we're going to do what we feel like we need to do even moving forward. Did we see that coming the other day? you know. Um, so but that's what you do. Uh, you learn from it, you own it, you fight like hell to fix it, and uh, you move on. >> My other question after the strip set the three play sequence, Judkins ran out of bounds to stop the clock, then two incomplete passes. Were you calling those plays or did change plays? >> No, I called those plays. Um ultimately we've got a puncture on the first run like it was not intended to bounce. Okay. So that one obviously we need to stay in bounds. Um the second one when we got nothing if if we puncture it uh we'd have been fine and we'd have stayed on track. Um if if if if I recall right, uh the second one we had an opportunity and and uh back-to-back plays we either got pressure or we got uh deflected ball and both of them we had opportunities to get the first down because at that point we certainly had to get close enough to get a field goal. I mean we weren't we weren't in field goal range yet. So at that moment um yeah I frustrated that we basically took about 20 seconds off the clock. Now in the end it gave us another possession. So, uh, there's two ways of looking at it. You can say, well, you were aggressive and it gave you another possession. Or you can look at and say, boy, you could have, you know, would I have liked to have driven the ball down, gotten all their timeouts left and gotten a touchdown or a field goal? Of course. But that was just a microcosm of our day of that that one part of it where we didn't execute at a high level and an opportunity with as as tough as a day as we had the touchdown and then the and then the fumble. We're right back to where we'd been the other three games with a chance to to finish it off in the fourth quarter. We didn't get it done which is the most frustrating thing of all. Hey Todd, another tackle question for you. Two and a half sacks for him over the last two games. Just uh what about his pass rush plan that he's put together have have you seen working really well? >> Well, he's relentless. I think that's he's got elite explosiveness off the ball. he was meant for attack style and his ability with the the varying pass rush moves is he's hard to handle if you're not going to slide to him and um it's been a credit to him coming back from the injury he had last year and uh he's he's explosive. he seems to always have the right the right mind frame and and uh and the ability to if he doesn't get a clean um release or if he doesn't get a clean get off or rush plan then he's he pushes the pocket. So uh been impressive to watch. I mean, I know his production has obviously increased on the stat sheet these last two weeks, but I mean, these these last handful of games, just with all the time he missed coming back from the quad, like do you think he's sort of hit another level after those first couple of games? >> Um, I don't I don't know about that about another level. Sometimes games present itself. Sometimes opportunities. Um, sometimes you win and the ball comes out quickly. Sometimes they're sliding to you. um, you know, the the the game itself, um, you know, it doesn't present itself. I I've always seen him as that player. I saw it last year. I voted for him. title: Kicking The Stigma : Strength in Every Story  Kelsey Mitchell
text: My mental health journey [music] has always kind of been a uphill, uphill, downhill battle. My father passed in 2024 [music] and I think that it kind of shifted my perspective. I think it exposed some of my vulnerabilities in terms of my relationship with God. >> [music] >> I think it exposed my relationship with my family and I think that a lot of times you go through bad things, it exposes how much you love yourself. And so, I [music] found out I need to kind of pour into myself a little bit more. You can tell people a million things about mental health and then [music] once it happens to you, you kind of get battle tested and you have to kind of figure out and adjust and be honest and look yourself in the mirror about where your mental health is. [music] I think mental health is important on every level, whether it be a 9-5 job, as an athlete, a 9-5 job working [music] as a computer wizard, it doesn't matter. I think that the reality is that we all go through stuff and I think that you have to accept that people have bad days. You can't act like or pretend that it's not happening to them or for them, especially when you know that it happens to you and for you a lot of times. [music] I think that you have to give people grace. I think that you have to be able to accept that people have bad days. [music] And I think you have to accept that in our in our world, in our society, that different things that people are hit with [music] different things every day and mental health and the telling of stories about mental health just is being vulnerable enough to say that, you know, >> I'm not having my best time right now or it's not the best, you know, best year, it's not the best month, it's not the best week, the best day and I think that that's okay [music] and I think that vulnerability is something that we as humans should be able to share with each other. I'm not too good to say that [music] I need help and I think that that should be something that all people should be okay with. It's like sometimes I just need a little help. It's not a negative thing. It's not a bad [music] thing. I think people hear mental health and they think something's wrong with them. Nah, it's just you taking care of yourself mentally. You're going to evolve. [music] You're going to find different things that you do and don't like. You're going to go through things that, you know, may not feel great to your spirit and to your heart, but I think at the end of the day it's like that's normal. [music] It lets you know that you're human. It lets you know that you can keep trying. I'm happy that I was able to withstand >> the bad days, the bad moments. I'm happy that I had a family to kind of do it with. It's strength in numbers, and so I always going to lean on the people around me that I know love me.

title: The NFL Suspends 49ers Linebacker Dre Greenlaw Without Pay for Week 6
text: Breaking news: Dre Greenlaw has been suspended without pay for the 49ers' next game against the Washington Commanders.  Uh, and this is because of his incident on the touchline where he headbutted Earnest Jones, who wasn't wearing a helmet. Uh, this means that Dre Greenlaw will essentially miss a game and a half because of that slight head injury.  And you might think that's a bit excessive , but the reason the NFL is so tough on him, and I don't blame them, is that he's a repeat offender.  This is not the first time he has hit a player very late out of bounds.  This is not the first time he has started a fight with the entire team on the sidelines. He is almost 30 years old.  He only has himself to blame.  Nothing he did was smart or helpful to the team.  Now, her passion, her emotion, the fury with which she plays is contagious, and the Niners need her. But at a certain point in his career he has to find the limit and stop crossing it because the NFL has no sympathy for him.  I mean, he really is the Draymond Green of the 49ers.  Draymond Green finds himself in the same situation.  The referees hate him.  The league uses him as an example, and he makes these mistakes at the worst possible time.  Greenlaw needs to avoid doing that.  They lost a Super Bowl not because he lost his temper, but because he tore his Achilles tendon .  They need him on the field.  They still use their absence as an excuse for why they lost.  They felt they would have won if he had been on the field.  So, don't take yourself out .  Thank God the Niners face the Washington Commanders next week and can win without him, but uh, you can't afford any more of these, Dre.  Let this be the last time.
